newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares gain half percent on strong dlr.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares gain half percent on strong dlr.

text.p: Hungarian share prices continued to gain ground on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday taking their power mostly from the dollar's strength, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,424.05 points, up 25.37.
"The dollar's strength was the number one factor to drive the market higher in the lack of any major corporate news," one trader said.
On the interbank market the Hungarian forint closed at 179.45/50 to the dollar, compared to Monday's close of 178.65/70.

Despite the gain in the index analysts believe the market's overall pattern has remained the same with many foreign investors standing on the sidelines waiting for fresh share offers or corporate developments.

"We still see very little business from international clients, they still seem to be just waiting for the market to develop some kind of real trend," said Frances Cloud, analyst at Nomura Equity Research in London.
Investors wait hoping they can get some oil company MOL, pharmaceuticals Richter and tile maker Zalakeramia shares more cheaply, she said.

The BUX futures market, generating a turnover of 1.80 billion forints, was mixed on Tuesday. June BUX edged up 4.50 points to 5,725, September was unchanged at 6,050, while the four other maturities fell by between 8.00 and 51.00 points.
On Tuesday, chemicals TVK remained the most actively traded stock which closed steady at 2,375 forints.

Borsodchem, which said that a court of appeal cleared it of illegal transport and disposal of hazardous waste for which it was earlier fined 20 million forints, advanced 25 forints to finish at 6,405.
Elsewhere, plastics group Pannonplast stocks rose 230 forints to end at 8,150, amid big orders, the trader said.
Most stocks remained rangebound but trading group Csopak's market was volatile as it traded between 2,720 and 3,000 forints, before closing at 2,800, down 50.
